summary: Parkdale, Sherwood and the edge of East Royalty: post-war Cape Cods and bungalows in Parkdale, 1960s-70s ranchers and split-levels in Sherwood's tree streets, a low commercial node at the five-legged 'Vogue Optical' roundabout, light industry along Belmont Street and the Confederation Trail, car dealers on Mount Edward Road and Allen Street, and the federal Experimental Farm's fields and ponds. Landmarks with photos: Cody Banks Arena (white metal barn, fieldstone entrance), the new net-zero Sherwood Elementary (2025), the blue Eastlink Centre, Ardgowan (cream Gothic cottage with green shutters), the rebuilt Harley Street apartments and the Plywood Place food bank.

buildings.name: Cody Banks Arena (Sherwood rink), off Maple Avenue
buildings.facts: City-owned rink, opened about 1966 (about 60 years old in 2026). Home to about 40 minor hockey teams, lacrosse; the Sherwood Lawn Bowling Club is behind it and the small Sherwood Recreation Hall is next to it. Jan 2026: city hired a consultant to plan a replacement 'Sherwood Sport and Recreation Complex'. Apr 16 2026 public meeting showed three options: keep the rink and build a new community centre ($20.4M), demolish and replace both ($53.8M), or a staged build ($57.2M). A condition report found it 'in good structural shape' with parts in poor shape, could last 15-20 years. Decision expected summer 2026; none reported yet. 2015: ammonia leak evacuated the building. Name stays.
buildings.look: A long, low barn: white ribbed metal siding on the long sides, a shallow gabled roof in light grey metal, no windows down the sides. The entrance at the gable end has a projecting gabled canopy (charcoal-grey soffit and fascia) on white posts with a slatted white screen, over a wall of tan-and-brown random fieldstone with glass double doors. 'Cody Banks Arena' in white italic letters on the canopy's dark gable. Gravel/asphalt lot in front with orange bollards.

buildings.name: Sherwood Elementary School (new, opened March 2025), Maple Avenue
buildings.facts: Built 2022-2025 on the site of the old school; groundbreaking July 18 2022, scheduled June 2024, opened to students March 26 2025 after repeated delays (students got extra spring and summer break days for the move). P.E.I.'s first net-zero-ready, all-electric school: solar panels, geothermal heat pumps, triple-pane glass; 650 students. The province didn't budget a playground; parents set out to raise $500,000 for one. The old red-brick school was to be demolished and its site made a playground. OSM has no lidar height (newer than 2020). East Royalty's new elementary (on the L.M. Montgomery site, done 2028) reuses this design.
buildings.look: Two-storey modern school in blocks: a base of dark charcoal split-face concrete block, upper walls in deep teal-green metal panels, with blocks clad in warm brown woodgrain panels and charcoal metal around a recessed glass entrance; other wings white/cream panels with yellow accent panels. Big window bands, flat roofs with solar panels. Gymnasium is the tallest block (teal over grey block).

buildings.name: Eastlink Centre (arena and trade centre), Kensington Road
buildings.facts: Built for the 1991 Canada Winter Games; home of the QMJHL Charlottetown Islanders; the city owns the arena half and the province the trade-centre half. Sept 2016: council deferred painting the faded exterior because the province hadn't been asked to pay for its half; the mayor said painting half would make it 'the building on Kensington Road that only one half of it is painted' ($80-100k for all). July 14 2026: a $54.9M modernization pitched to the federal finance minister: seats from 4,000 to 5,000+, walking track, emergency shelter for 1,000+; the city agreed to cover interest on an ~$18M loan. No construction yet.
buildings.look: A big box: upper walls of royal-blue ribbed metal siding over a red-brown brick base about 3 m high. buildings.name: Ardgowan National Historic Site (house), 2 Palmers Lane
buildings.facts: Victorian cottage of William Henry Pope (Father of Confederation), who hosted Charlottetown Conference delegates to a luncheon there in 1864. National Historic Site 1966, bought by Parks Canada 1967; the house is Parks Canada offices (not open inside); the grounds and gardens are public. 2019: $304,000 restoration of the 1860s gardens, ~50 of 500+ trees removed, new wooden fences and gates, site hooked to city sewer (was septic). Two Parks Canada EV chargers in the lot.
buildings.look: A rambling 1.5-storey Gothic-cottage: cream/off-white board-and-batten siding, steep cross gables with white bargeboards, bright green louvered shutters, dark burgundy window sashes, bay windows, a long verandah with tan posts and scroll brackets between the wings, dark brown-grey shingle roof, tall cream corbelled chimneys (about four). Set back in lawns and big old trees.

buildings.name: Ravenwood (Experimental Farm house), 15 Crown Drive
buildings.facts: Federally recognized heritage building ('Building 5' of the Experimental Farm): built about 1820-1828 (granted to Attorney General William Johnstone in 1820); the farm (est. 1909) was planned around it and its directors lived in it. Now offices (Island Nature Trust has been a tenant). Lidar eave 5.7 m, ridge 9.6 m.

buildings.name: Experimental Farm greenhouses (Agriculture Canada), off Allen Street
buildings.facts: Part of the Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada research farm (35 ha between Belvedere Avenue and Allen Street, est. 1909): research station buildings along University Avenue, test fields, community gardens, ponds (the 'lily pond') and the Confederation Trail. 2002 declared surplus then kept; 2023 Mayor Philip Brown floated housing on it for the federal Housing Accelerator Fund pitch; MP Sean Casey called it the city's 'crown jewel'; Friends of the Farm (100+ members) oppose; the Mi'kmaq want to be consulted and have said they'd like to acquire it. The OSM greenhouse block is 9,157 m², 3.4-6.5 m.

neighbourhoods.name: Parkdale
neighbourhoods.where: former town (amalgamated 1995), between Allen Street/Kensington Road in the south and Belvedere Avenue in the north, St Peters Road on the east, Mount Edward Road on the west
neighbourhoods.look: 1940s-60s post-war suburb: 1.5-storey Cape Cods and storey-and-a-half houses with dormers, bungalows on small lots, mature maples. neighbourhoods.where: north of Belvedere Avenue, between Mount Edward Road and St Peters Road, up to the bypass (Maple, Pine, Cedar, Poplar, Sycamore Avenues: the tree streets)
neighbourhoods.look: 1960s-70s suburb: bungalows, split-levels and raised ranchers (e.g. a 'well-built 3 bedroom rancher' on Centennial Drive), big lawns; vinyl siding in beige, white, grey, light green; some brick-front bungalows. Commercial node at the St Peters/Brackley Point roundabout: low plazas, gas stations, Tim's. Infill apartments since 2020 (41-unit Pine Drive block approved June 2020 against planning board advice).

neighbourhoods.name: East Royalty
neighbourhoods.where: east of St Peters Road north of the bypass toward the Hillsborough River (Falconwood, Gordon, Norwood Roads)
neighbourhoods.look: Mix of 1970s-90s split-levels and bungalows and 2005-2025 subdivisions: two-storey vinyl houses and semi-detached in grey, greige, white, navy accents, black shingles; townhouse rows; 20-unit walk-ups (6 Elena Court burned 2024). Very new streets have small trees. New East Royalty Elementary being built on the L.M. Montgomery school site (2025-2028).

neighbourhoods.name: Belmont Street / Plywood Place / Longworth Avenue
neighbourhoods.where: south of Allen Street along the Confederation Trail
neighbourhoods.look: Light industry: metal-sided garages, auto electric, parts, the food bank; older 1.5-storey houses on Longworth; the Second Empire funeral home.

neighbourhoods.name: Mount Edward Road apartment strip

neighbourhoods.look: Car dealers at the south end; new 4-6 storey apartment blocks near the bypass (St. Martha's Court area); Ellis and Birt proposed three more buildings (87 units) at the bypass, Jan 2026, rendering shows 5-6 storeys in beige/brown and white panels.

current_events.what: Eastlink Centre paint saga: Sept 2016 council deferred painting the faded arena because the province owns the other half; mayor: painting half would make it 'the building on Kensington Road that only one half of it is painted'. July 2026: $54.9M renovation pitched; 'we're not looking for a grant, we're looking for an investment'.

Cody Banks Arena: three replacement options from $20.4M to $57.2M (Apr 2026); councillor wants it to beat the new Simmons centre ('raise the standard'); the cheapest option keeps the 60-year-old rink.
New Sherwood Elementary, net-zero, opened March 2025 after a 'moving target' opening date (planned June 2024); province didn't budget a playground, parents raising $500,000.

Experimental farm: Mayor offered it for housing in a Housing Accelerator Fund pitch (Dec 2023); MP calls it the 'crown jewel'; Friends of the Farm: 'if they can keep 840 acres in Central Park... they can keep 80 acres'. Declared surplus 2002, un-surplused later.
Third fire hall: land bought 2017, plan changed 2019 after Sherwood objected, paused 2023, $6M of ~$12M budgeted 2026; 'let's build it, then we'll staff'. Station 2 Sherwood is all-volunteer.

Pine Drive 41-unit apartments approved June 2020 against the planning board and staff ('significantly out of context'); developer tried since 2012; two councillors in conflict of interest left the room.
current_events.where: Pine Drive off Mount Edward Road, near Sherwood Elementary

current_events.what: Charlottetown's new official plan (2025-26) lets buildings go to 10 storeys along busy streets like St Peters Road; fire union notes taller buildings, same crew of three.
Harley Street apartment fire July 2019 (cigarette in mulch, balcony barbecue propane); rebuilt taller with balcony sprinklers; 3 of 52 tenants returned.
Upper Room food bank moved 'a couple hundred feet' to a bigger building, Nov 2024; ~1,100 families a month.
St Peters Road and the bypass: 45,000+ vehicles a day; Canada's first displaced left turn (Oct 2020) after studying a roundabout, overpass and 'jug handle'; inspired by Salt Lake City.
current_events.where: St Peters Road at the bypass
